I've posted the design for LIN-4447 to Linear as a comment, and written the chosen approach into the description below the unchanged `## As asked` block. The ticket stays In Progress. This was a design stage, so there's no PR, commit or test run.

**Is the ticket still accurate?** Yes. Nothing under `lib/`, `routes/`, `tests/` or `docs/areas/` has changed since the ticket was filed, and I read every file it names at `origin/main` `4b5001ddf`.

**The cause:** every screen and check works out close-out readiness again from the raw comments, so each rule has copies. I found one copy the two surveys missed: `deriveState` in `lib/run-evidence.js` is a second, looser close-out box built from the same PRs. That makes six places deciding close-out (the surveys counted five), plus three different readers of "this task's PRs".

**Options weighed:**
- **Fix each case where it shows:** rejected. It leaves the copies in place, and patching `closeOutSetsDone` would reverse John's passenger ruling.
- **Store readiness once per task:** rejected. A stored answer goes stale when the project changes outside Harbour, which is exactly why the passenger ruling exists.
- **Chosen: one close-out decision and one reading of the comment trail, called by every surface.**

**The pieces, sizes varied and leaning larger:**
- **0, before any code:** blind reads of Runs & dispatch and of an untouched control area (`front-end-pages`), taken in the same window on one rubric, repeated at the end. No area-level read tool exists in the repo, and without this baseline the last "Done when" can't be judged.
- **1, larger:** `closeOutDecision` plus a `CLOSE_OUT_REASONS` constant in precedence order. It writes the passenger rule once, retires `REFUSED_REASONS` and the extra `closeOutWaitsOn` calls, and adds a test proving the rule is written once.

(assistant-text 2/2)
- **2, larger:** a new `lib/run-trail.js` holding the one comment classifier and one rule for which PRs belong to a task. An agent note that cites a new PR after review now sends the task back to review, which fixes the Seams §3.0a case. I chose that over dropping agent notes from the count, because that would leave an unreviewed PR outside the gate. The classifier boundary needs agreement with A14.
- **3, small:** `dispatchModelOf` is retired; the timeline reads the model the cost fold already picks.
- **4, medium:** the live-stage wait moves to `lib/run-live-wait.js`, a Runs-owned file, and the old file is deleted rather than kept as a re-export.
- **5 to 7, medium and small:** single homes for the halt modes and feedback kinds, the `dispatch-factory` test check, and splitting the call reads out of `cost-read.js`.

**Waiting entries:** of the 20, 12 are settled by pieces 1–7. The other 8 now say why they can't be settled yet and whose decision they wait on; four of those are copies in simple-dispatcher. No part of the "As asked" block is cut.

**Two rulings John needs to make, each with my recommendation:**
- **R1, passenger scope:** does "Harbour is a passenger" cover both a person marking Done and a merge made outside Harbour? I recommend yes to both. Piece 1 waits on this; pieces 0, 2, 3 and 4 don't.
- **R2, simple-dispatcher:** may this task change it? I recommend no: open one follow-up ticket for a shared contract across both repos instead. The same ruling covers stored pre-cutover paragraphs, where I recommend keeping them as written and marking them pre-cutover.
